staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 02 reviewed this exact prepared HTSlib snapshot. Its `cram/cram_encode.c:3097-3104` vulnerable `case 'B'` logic matches the saved ASan trace and the staged fix hunk exactly, even though the local head is newer than the metadata vulnerable commit and includes unrelated harness-side changes.

bug_description.original: Detailed Report: https://oss-fuzz.com/testcase?key=6707644370649088 Project: htslib Fuzzing Engine: afl Fuzz Target: hts_open_fuzzer Job Type: afl_asan_htslib Crash Type: Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 Crash State: process_one_read cram_encode_container cram_flush_container_mt Sanitizer: address (ASAN).
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json issue_description / staged sanitizer_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged witness is a 99-byte BAM file beginning `42 41 4d 01`. `bam_hdr_read()` first reads `l_text = 0` and `n_targets = 1`, so the sanitized header later presented to the CRAM writer has no `M5` tags. During `sam_hdr_write(out, hdr)` for CRAM output, `cram_write_SAM_hdr()` cannot find reference data and sets `fd->embed_ref = 2`, matching the saved `cram_write_SAM_hdr` warnings. The only alignment record then reaches `bam_read1()`, which reads `block_len = 73` and core fields `tid = 0`, `l_qname = 2`, `n_cigar = 9`, `l_qseq = 0`; because the raw qname bytes are `20 20`, `fixup_missing_qname_nul()` and qname padding raise the in-memory qname length to 4 while leaving `b->l_data = 43`. That layout makes `bam_ref(b) == 0` and `bam_get_l_aux(b) == 3`, with auxiliary bytes `20 ff 42`: two raw tag-name bytes followed immediately by aux type `B` and no subtype or count bytes. When the first CRAM container is created for this record, it inherits the earlier `embed_ref == 2` state. In `process_one_read()`, `bam_aux_get()` walks the malformed aux blob, `skip_aux()` rejects the truncated `B` tag, and both `MD` and `NM` lookups fail, producing `cf_tag = 3`. Vulnerable `cram_encode_aux()` then computes `aux_size == 3`, copies those three bytes into a temporary heap buffer, and appends synthetic `cFC\x03`, yielding the 7-byte allocation reported by AddressSanitizer. The `case 'B'` parser checks only `aux_end - aux < 3+4`, so this 7-byte buffer is accepted even though a valid `B` tag header needs 8 bytes. The subsequent `count` assembly reads `aux[7]` as the missing high count byte, one byte past the allocation, producing the reproduced AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow read at `cram_encode.c:3104`. The fix changes the guard to `4+4`, rejecting this exact truncated-B-tag witness before the out-of-bounds read.

source.description: First project parser statement that consumes attacker-controlled BAM header metadata and creates the header state later used to auto-enable `embed_ref=2` on the CRAM output path.
source.value_from: In the staged witness the BAM header has `l_text = 0` and `n_targets = 1`. After `sam_hdr_sanitise()` this yields a header with one reference entry but no `M5` tags, which later drives `cram_write_SAM_hdr()` into its `fd->embed_ref = 2` auto-embed branch when reference loading fails.

root_cause.description: The vulnerable `B`-tag length check requires only seven remaining bytes before reading a subtype byte and a four-byte element count. On the reproduced path the temporary aux buffer has exactly seven bytes, so this guard falls through even though a valid `B` header needs eight bytes.
root_cause.note: The staged fix changes this check to `4+4`, which is the missing source-level obligation for this bug.

sink.description: AddressSanitizer crash site. `cram_encode_aux()` reads the fourth count byte `aux[7]` while assembling the `B`-array element count from a 7-byte heap buffer.
sink.note: The saved ASan trace reports `READ of size 1` at `cram_encode.c:3104:42` and says the address is 0 bytes to the right of the 7-byte region allocated at `cram_encode.c:2775`.

tainted_value_origin.description: This is where the parsed BAM layout from `bam_read1()` is collapsed into the scalar auxiliary extent that sizes the temporary heap copy. With `b->l_data = 43`, `b->core.n_cigar = 9`, `b->core.l_qname = 4`, and `b->core.l_qseq = 0`, `bam_get_l_aux(b)` becomes 3 and `bam_aux(b)` points at `20 ff 42`.

parser_admitted.description: Because the witness begins with `BAM\1`, `sam_hdr_read()` dispatches into `bam_hdr_read()` rather than the SAM or CRAM readers. This is the format-admission point for the source step.

evidence_limitations: The prepared source snapshot used for Stage 02 grounding is local commit `9e1ffd856614fcfc0bb3b89501600827cc8705e7`, not the metadata vulnerable commit `61b037bb881e85259f8df30c78d99ad3a357ed52`. The trace therefore cites exact lines from the staged snapshot that reproduced the crash and whose vulnerable `case 'B'` hunk matches the staged fix diff.

The saved artifacts prove that `aux[7]` is one byte past the 7-byte heap copy, but ASan stops at that read and does not provide the redzone byte value. The trace therefore records only the out-of-bounds fetch itself, not any concrete assembled `count` or downstream `blen`.

The `fd->embed_ref = 2` prerequisite is grounded by the staged `cram_write_SAM_hdr()` source and the saved Stage 01 warnings; `run_flags.json` sets `runtime_disambiguation` to `false`, so no extra instrumentation was used to observe that branch.

coarse_trace.summary: The BAM parser admits the 99-byte witness. `bam_hdr_read()` materializes an empty-text header with one reference and no `M5` tags, and `bam_read1()` later materializes one malformed record with `block_len = 73`, `tid = 0`, `b->l_data = 43`, final padded `l_qname = 4`, and a 3-byte aux blob `20 ff 42`.

On the CRAM output path, `cram_write_SAM_hdr()` uses that header state to enable `fd->embed_ref = 2`; when the first CRAM container is created for the malformed record, it inherits that state, and the malformed aux blob makes the `MD` and `NM` lookups fail so `cf_tag = 3`.
The encoder computes `aux_size == 3`, copies the truncated aux bytes, and appends synthetic `cFC\x03`, creating the 7-byte heap buffer reported by AddressSanitizer.
The `case 'B'` guard checks only `3+4` bytes, so the 7-byte buffer is accepted and the count assembly reads `aux[7]` one byte past the allocation.

fine_trace.note: Source. `bam_hdr_read()` consumes the BAM header metadata here. For this witness `h->l_text = 0` and `h->n_targets = 1`, so the sanitized header later handed to the CRAM writer has one reference entry but no `M5` tags.

During `sam_hdr_write(out, hdr)` on the CRAM output path, `cram_write_SAM_hdr()` iterates the header derived from step 1, finds no `M5` tag for the reference, and `cram_get_ref(fd, i, 1, rlen)` fails in the saved run. Because `fd->embed_ref == -1`, this branch logs `No M5 tags present and could not find reference` / `Enabling embed_ref=2 option` and sets `fd->embed_ref = 2`.

After step 1 has consumed the BAM header and reference table, `bam_read1()` starts consuming the only alignment record. The first 4 bytes decode to `block_len = 73`, and the following 32-byte read captures the BAM core words that determine the record layout later used by the CRAM writer.

fine_trace.var: c->tid, c->l_qname, c->l_extranul, c->n_cigar, c->l_qseq, new_l_data
fine_trace.note: The core words from step 3 decode to the load-bearing record fields on this path: `tid = 0`, `l_qname = 2`, `l_extranul = 2`, `n_cigar = 9`, and `l_qseq = 0`. From `block_len = 73`, `new_l_data` becomes `73 - 32 + 2 = 43`.
The in-memory BAM record buffer is resized to `new_l_data` and fixed at `b->l_data = 43`, establishing the eventual extent that `bam_get_l_aux(b)` will subtract against.

The raw qname bytes are `20 20`, so the second byte is not NUL. Because `c->l_extranul > 0`, `fixup_missing_qname_nul()` writes `\0` at `b->data[2]`, increments `c->l_qname` from 2 to 3, and decrements `c->l_extranul` from 2 to 1 instead of reallocating again.

One remaining padding byte is zero-filled, so the final in-memory qname length becomes `c->l_qname = 4`. `bam_read1()` then copies the remaining 39 bytes into `b->data + 4`, leaving the record with `bam_ref(b) == 0` from step 4 and a final aux tail `20 ff 42`; with `b->l_data = 43`, `n_cigar = 9`, and `l_qseq = 0`, the later `bam_get_l_aux(b)` calculation is therefore `43 - 36 - 4 = 3`.

When the first CRAM container is created for this record, `cram_put_bam_seq()` copies step 2's `fd->embed_ref == 2` state into `fd->ctr->embed_ref`. The local `embed_ref` later tested in `process_one_read()` comes from this container field.

With the copied `embed_ref == 2` state from step 8, `process_one_read()` probes the malformed aux blob for `MD` and `NM`. On the three-byte aux payload from step 7, `skip_aux()` in `sam.c:4677-4682` reaches `case 'B'`, sees fewer than 5 bytes after the type byte, and returns NULL; `bam_aux_get()` therefore logs `Corrupted aux data for read` and returns NULL for both lookups. The auto-reference bitmask becomes `cf_tag = 3`.

Tainted value origin. The parsed BAM layout from steps 4-7 is converted into the scalar aux extent here: `bam_get_l_aux(b)` evaluates to 3 because `b->l_data = 43`, `n_cigar = 9`, `l_qname = 4`, and `l_qseq = 0`. `orig == aux` points at the three aux bytes `20 ff 42`, so `aux[2]` is the truncated `B` type code.

Because `cf_tag` is nonzero on this pre-CRAM4 path, the encoder copies the 3-byte malformed aux blob to a temporary heap buffer and appends synthetic `cFC\x03`. The active aux span therefore grows from 3 bytes to exactly 7 bytes, matching the 7-byte allocation range reported by AddressSanitizer from this `malloc(aux_size+4)` site.

Root cause. In the `case 'B'` path, this guard requires only seven remaining bytes. Step 11 made `aux_end - aux == 7`, so the malformed tag survives the check even though a valid `B` header needs eight bytes: 2 tag bytes, type `B`, subtype, and a 4-byte count.

After step 12 falls through, the `B`-tag parser reuses the appended `cFC\x03` bytes as the subtype and low three count bytes, then fetches `aux[7]` as the missing high count byte. But the copied aux buffer from step 11 is only 7 bytes long, so `aux[7]` is the first byte past the allocation.
Sink. AddressSanitizer reports the 1-byte heap-buffer-overflow read at this fourth count-byte fetch: the faulting address is exactly 0 bytes past the 7-byte heap region allocated in step 11.

allocation_context.note: ASan attributes the over-read buffer to the temporary `malloc(aux_size+4)` copy used only when `cf_tag` is appended. On the witnessed record, `aux_size == 3`, so this allocation is the 7-byte region `[0x602000005270,0x602000005277)` from the saved trace.

poc.trigger: The staged 99-byte `poc` begins with `BAM\1`, so `hts_open_fuzzer` routes it through `view_sam(data, size, "wc")`. On that CRAM path `sam_hdr_write(out, hdr)` first auto-enables `embed_ref=2`, then the single malformed alignment is buffered, and `hts_close(out)` reproduces the `AddressSanitizer: heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1` in `cram_encode_aux()` while CRAM encoding its truncated `B` aux tag.

format.name: 99-byte BAM file with an empty-text header and one record whose aux section is a truncated `B` tag
format.contract: A BAM file whose header yields no `M5` tags on the reproduced CRAM path, causing `cram_write_SAM_hdr()` to set `embed_ref=2`, and whose only alignment record reaches the CRAM writer with `bam_get_l_aux(b) == 3` and aux bytes `20 ff 42`, so `process_one_read()` appends the synthetic `cFC` tag, `cram_encode_aux()` sees exactly seven bytes in the current `case 'B'` span, passes `if (aux_end - aux < 3+4)`, and then reads the nonexistent eighth header byte `aux[7]` while assembling `count`. No broader truncated-B-tag family is asserted beyond this witnessed BAM-to-CRAM path.
